key_points: IBM scientists propose a new communication model that incorporates the receiver's ability to reason and deduce facts.
The framework introduces 'logical semantic entropy' to measure communication limits when logical deduction is possible.
The study reveals that correcting a receiver's incorrect beliefs can become infinitely more costly than informing them of unknown facts.
The authors suggest this approach is vital for modern AI systems that process and reason over information.
items.summary: IBM Research scientists published a paper in PNAS proposing a communication framework that explicitly accounts for logical deduction. The team extends Claude Shannon's 1948 model by giving receivers reasoning capabilities to infer additional facts from transmitted data. They derived a new quantity called 'logical semantic entropy' to define communication limits under these conditions. The researchers identified three key findings: the 'No Need to Know' result, the 'Less Is More' paradox regarding data efficiency versus security, and the high cost of correcting mistaken beliefs. The authors argue this richer theory is essential for future intelligent systems that depend on reasoning over information.
items.title: IBM Researchers Propose New Communication Theory Accounting for Reasoning

key_points: IBM Research and UC Berkeley applied MAST to analyze 310 ITBench traces from three distinct model classes.
Frontier models fail with isolated bottlenecks while large open models suffer from cascading failure modes.
Incorrect verification is the strongest predictor of failure across all tested models.
MAST converts unstructured execution logs into structured failure signatures to guide targeted engineering fixes.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: IBM Research and UC Berkeley collaborated to analyze why agentic large language models fail during real-world IT automation tasks. The researchers applied MAST, a Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy, to 310 ITBench SRE traces generated by Gemini-3-Flash, Kimi-K2, and GPT-OSS-120B. Their analysis revealed that frontier models like Gemini-3-Flash exhibit isolated bottlenecks, whereas large open models suffer from cascading failures. A primary driver of failure across all models was incorrect verification, where agents declared success without checking ground truth. Kimi-K2 struggled significantly with premature termination and failing to recognize when tasks were complete. GPT-OSS-120B demonstrated severe instability, frequently losing conversation history and disconnecting reasoning from actions. The authors report that externalizing verification and moving termination logic outside the model are critical fixes. They emphasize that simple success metrics are insufficient for engineering robust systems, as they do not explain the specific reasons for failure. MAST converts unstructured execution logs into structured failure signatures, allowing developers to identify precise interventions rather than resorting to blind prompting tweaks.
items.title: IBM and UC Berkeley Diagnose Enterprise Agent Failures Using MAST and ITBench

key_points: Databricks states that GPU failures are expected at scale, making rapid automatic recovery essential for maintaining high goodput.
PyTorch's distributed checkpoint API allows parallel writes across ranks, significantly reducing the time GPUs spend saving state.
An overlapped input pipeline caches data on local NVMe storage to prevent GPUs from idling while waiting for remote files.

items.summary: Databricks explains that training efficiency relies on maximizing GPU goodput by minimizing downtime from failures and data starvation. The article details how PyTorch's distributed checkpoint API enables parallel saves, reducing idle time and allowing frequent recovery points. Additionally, an overlapped input pipeline caches data locally to prevent GPUs from waiting on remote storage. These strategies ensure that hardware failures become minor interruptions rather than job-ending events, maintaining high computational throughput even on unreliable clusters.
items.title: Databricks optimizes PyTorch training with fault-tolerant checkpoints and data pipelines

key_points: Lakebase Postgres decouples compute and storage layers to optimize for agent workloads.
The system uses the Postgres write-ahead log as the durable source of truth stored on object storage.
Database copies and restores become cheap pointers to specific log sequence numbers.
Agents can create isolated branches instantly without duplicating large volumes of data.
Point-in-time recovery allows reverting to any past state by referencing an earlier log entry.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: Lakebase Postgres introduces a database architecture that decouples compute from storage to optimize performance for AI agents. The system treats the Postgres write-ahead log as the primary source of truth rather than traditional data files. By storing the transaction timeline on cheap object storage, the platform allows database copies and restores to function as lightweight pointers instead of expensive data migrations. The architecture enables instant branching of large databases by creating references to specific log sequence numbers rather than duplicating pages. Agents can execute migrations on isolated branches without impacting production systems, ensuring safe experimentation at scale. Point-in-time recovery becomes a simple operation of pointing to an earlier log entry, eliminating the need for full data restoration. This design leverages the immutable nature of object storage to maintain a complete history of every database change efficiently.
items.title: Lakebase Postgres uses object storage and WAL for agent workloads

items.summary: Photographer Jingna Zhang and her team maintain Cara, a platform designed to protect artists from unauthorized AI training data. Despite implementing filters, the site suffered three major scrapes this month, exposing millions of images and personal metadata. The initial scraper, a student known as Heft, later apologized and agreed to collaborate with Zhang. Heft, who admitted his actions were cruel, now helps identify platform vulnerabilities. Together, they are developing Lantern, an open-source tool that notifies artists if their work appears in public datasets. Zhang hopes this incident will prompt policymakers to address the broader issue of data harvesting beyond copyright law.
items.title: Cara Creator Collaborates With Former Scraper On New Artist Protection Tool

key_points: Tim O'Brien states that token volume does not capture whether an AI workload was worth completing.
The author compares AI token accounting to database FinOps, noting that cost metrics fail without context on purpose and architecture.
O'Brien warns that vendors selling simple optimization ideas ignore how model selection and failure impact total economics.
The article concludes that future AI financial management must connect consumption to workflow quality and business outcomes.
items.summary: Tim O'Brien argues that measuring AI productivity solely by token volume is a flawed approach that ignores whether work was actually valuable. He compares this error to FinOps blind spots regarding databases, where cost alone does not justify expense without understanding purpose and architecture. The author warns that vendors promoting simple token optimization miss critical questions about model selection, task complexity, and failure consequences. O'Brien notes that a cheap model causing retries can cost more than an expensive one succeeding immediately, and that different tasks require different architectural approaches. He suggests the future of AI financial management lies in connecting consumption to business outcomes rather than just counting tokens.
items.title: Tokens Are Not Dollars: Why AI Cost Metrics Fail to Measure Value

items.title: BloombergNEF reports $25 billion solar-plus-storage investment in first half of 2026

key_points: Scientists at the Centre for Ecological Sciences, Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, report that closely-related Western Ghats frogs living together tend to differ in body size.
The study found this pattern especially evident in endemic Nyctibatrachus and Micrixalus genera, where coexisting species showed significant size differences.
First author Kartik Shanker explains this results from competition and species sorting, allowing dissimilar species to coexist while excluding those with similar traits.
Researchers noted larger Nyctibatrachus frogs occupy faster-flowing stream sections while smaller species hide in leaf litter.
However, the study found no strong evidence that competition directly drove the evolution of body size, suggesting the pattern operates more at an ecological than evolutionary scale.

The study found this pattern especially evident in endemic Nyctibatrachus and Micrixalus genera, where coexisting species showed significant size differences. First author Kartik Shanker explains this results from competition and species sorting, allowing dissimilar species to coexist while excluding those with similar traits. Researchers noted larger Nyctibatrachus frogs occupy faster-flowing stream sections while smaller species hide in leaf litter. However, the study found no strong evidence that competition directly drove the evolution of body size, suggesting the pattern operates more at an ecological than evolutionary scale. Shanker warns that changes to microhabitats could threaten species even when broader forest habitats remain intact.
items.title: Western Ghats frogs sort by size to coexist, study finds

She has recently engaged with student protests and proposed a scheme to provide Rs.40,000 annually to women. The author argues her presence allows the SP to question National Crime Records Bureau data showing rising serious offences and crimes against women since 2017. With young voters comprising roughly 21.19 per cent of Uttar Pradesh's electorate, the author suggests Dimple's modern image could bridge gaps with Gen Z. The piece concludes that her role might transform the 2027 contest into a debate over which party better addresses women and youth concerns.

key_points: Thirty-five individuals in Jhabrera constituency allege their identities were forged to file 1,657 objections against Muslim voters.
Most of these applicants are BJP booth-level agents who have since submitted affidavits denying involvement.

Former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa recommended an inquiry into fraudulent objection filings.
The Election Commission has cancelled the objections after applicants withdrew them, but the misuse remains unexplained.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: In Uttarakhand's Jhabrera constituency, 35 individuals claim their identities were misused to file 1,657 objections against Muslim voters during the electoral roll revision. Most of these applicants are BJP booth-level agents who submitted affidavits stating their names, EPIC numbers, and signatures were forged. While polling officials say the matter lies with the complainants, former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa argued for an official inquiry into fraudulent filings. The Election Commission has cancelled the objections after the applicants withdrew them, but no investigation has been launched into how the misuse occurred. This incident follows a broader pattern in the state where high-volume Form 7 applications targeted Muslim voters. Local residents affected by these forged applications expressed confusion and frustration, noting they received no prior notice. Despite the withdrawals, the underlying issue of identity misuse remains unresolved, raising concerns about the integrity of the special intensive revision process.
items.title: Uttarakhand SIR: BJP agents' 'forged' objections against Muslim voters remain unsolved

items.summary: ABP Majha journalist Mandar Gonjari was named in three FIRs following a campus clash at the College of Engineering Pune. The conflict arose after Gonjari interviewed students about their plans to attend Rahul Gandhi's event and a subsequent dispute over a scholarship grievance. Gonjari alleges ABVP activists pressured a student to retract her comments, while the college administration claims NSUI and Congress workers trespassed and created fear. Gonjari denies entering the hostel and maintains his reporting was conducted in an open area.
items.title: ABP journalist booked after Pune college clash over student interview
